name: One
description: As an element, the character will retain its original meaning of one, and can occasionally represent either a ceiling or a floor, depending on where the element is written within the kanji.

name: Five
description: This somewhat rare element will carry the meaning of 'five', and will also carry its on reading of ゴ.

name: Seven
description: As an element, this kanji references something being cut up into seven pieces. Note how the second stroke cuts through the first? You may wonder to yourself 'why seven pieces?' It is best not to dwell on such questions in life.

name: Eight
description: As an element, the kanji retains the meaning of 'eight' and also represents something which has been split in half, relating to the many times the number eight can be divided.

name: Nine
description: As an element, keep the idea of 'nine' in mind, such as with the nine-player game baseball. This element is very similar to 丸 but is of course missing the short 'drop' stroke. In the same way that nine is 'not quite ten', this retains the feeling of something that is 'not quite' complete.

name: Ten
description: As an element, it's easy to extend the idea of 'ten' to that of a 'cross'.

name: Mouth
description: As an element, extend the idea of 'mouth' to any opening, such as a doorway, river mouth etc.

name: Sun
description: As an element, this can mean either 'sun' or 'day'.

name: Moon
description: This element can either mean 'moon', or 'body part' and appears in the kanji for many anatmocical features.

name: Evening
description: This element will retain its meaning of 'evening'

name: Rice Field
description: As an element, keep the meaning of 'rice field'.

name: Tree
description: As an element, the idea of 'tree' is also extended to 'wood' and all things wooden.

name: Mountain
description: As an element, keep the idea of a very large 'mountain', not just a small hill.

name: Stone
description: As an element, keep the idea of 'stone' and use it to include any object made of stone.

name: Eye
description: This kanji keeps the meaning of 'eye' when used as an element.

name: Shellfish
description: Though this element still retains the idea of 'shellfish', it also extends to the idea of 'money'. One can imagine that before modern coin minting procedures, people used seashells when trading for goods and services.

name: Power
description: It might be easier to think of this element as representing the flexing arm of someone with immense physical 'power'. Be sure not to mix this up with 刀 and the previously encountered element 九.

name: Say
description: As an element, use 'say' or 'words' when creating stories.

name: Old
description: Despite being made up of two pre-existing elements, this too can be used as an element and carries the same meaning of 'old'. Despite the tombstone symbolism, try to avoid linking with this element with the idea of 'death' or a 'grave' as these elements associated with these will be introduced later.

name: Drop
description: Here we have a single drop of something, perhaps a drop of water or ink, created with a single stroke. The 'drop' can be written both left to right and right to left depending on the kanji. We will notice a few instances where the only difference between two kanji is the existence (or lack) of a single drop.

name: White
description: As an element, maintain the idea of white, though it may be easier to think of something that is itself white.

name: Hundred
description: As an element, imagine the idea of something being 100%.

name: Walking Stick
description: We've already seen the horizontal version of this element. The single vertical line can have a variety of meanings when used as an element, for example, a walking stick, a column, or sometimes a stake driving through something.

name: Thousand
description: As an element, keep the idea of a thousand where it makes sense to, though it may be easier to view this element pictorally as some sort of stake being forced into the top something when this element is seen above something else.

name: Middle
description: This form carries the same meaning of 'middle' when used as an element.

name: Small
description: The element keeps the same meaning and commonly appears above or below other elements. When appearing at the top of a kanji, the outer drops instead hook inwards. We will continue to encounter elements whose shape change depending on the kanji.

name: Few
description: This form also appears as an element, and again takes on the meaning of 'a few' of something.

name: Magic Wand
description: A pole with a drop coming off it must be a magic wand. You can almost see the magic sparkles coming right off it.

name: Stop
description: This kanji originally took the form of a footprint, though it has become heavily abstracted with time. As an element, extend the idea of 'stop' to something which has 'stopped dead in its tracks'.

name: Correct
description: Keep the idea of correctness when using this element.

name: Oneself
description: We will meet many elements associated with people, so it might be better to consider this element as 'nose'. We will meet the full kanji for nose where this element appears, 鼻, much later.

name: Mother
description: As an element, this form retains the idea of motherhood.

name: Lie Down
description: A drop and a horizontal stroke creates the image of someone lying down in a bed with one leg slipping down off the side.

name: Each
description: As an element, this form takes the meaning of 'each' or 'every'. Note how the two 'drops' inside the 'mother' component are combined together into a single stroke.

name: Father
description: As with mother, this element represents the idea of fatherhood.

name: Pot Lid
description: The shape of a pot lid should be quite easy to make out here, see the handle represented by the first stroke? Occasionally, it might also be easier to think of this element as a 'top hat'.

name: Mingle
description: The element here should also conjur up the idea of people mingling about.

name: Person
description: Be careful when using this element. It might be a good idea to ascribe this to a single, specific person rather than a general idea as there are many elements associated with people.

name: Water
description: The element for water is another one of those shape shifting elements. It is often seen on the left-hand side where it is reduced to just three strokes.

name: Ice
description: As with 'water', the element for ice is also reduced down, but this time even further to just two strokes. As with water, it normally appears on the left-hand side of the kanji.

name: Gully
description: Previously we discussed how the element for eight '八' could represent something split in two. Here we see a gully that has been eroded by running water and the mouth representing the water running through it.

name: Guillotine
description: Here the person we encountered a few frames earlier has met an unfortunate demise, with their head about to be chopped off by a guillotine represented by the first two strokes.

name: Fire
description: As an element, this form can take the meaning of 'fire', 'flames' or anything on fire. The element often appears either on the left-hand side or bottom of the kanji. However, when it appears at the bottom, it is often reduced to four 'drop'-like strokes.

name: Heart
description: As an element, this form often appears in kanji related to thoughts and emotions and can take on the meaning of 'heart' or 'feeling'. When it appears on the left hand side, it is reduced to just three strokes. It may be worthwhile to attach a slightly different meaning to the form when it appears in its three stroke form, such as one's 'state of mind' to differentiate it from the four stroke variant 'heart'. This element can be tricky to create pneumonics with due to the relatively abstract nature of many of the kanji that it appears as part of. For this reason, make sure your pnemonics are especially strong and unusual.

name: Bamboo
description: This element often appears at the top of the kanji, occupying the same position as the 'grass' element would. This is another example of an element that changes form slightly, often having the long stalks reduced to mere drops.

name: Thread
description: This element is often used for kanji to do with textiles, fabrics and thin objects. However, this also extends to more abstract ideas of tying and joining things together. When this element appears on the left side, some of it's strokes are shortened in a similar way to tree and fire elements.

name: Lineage
description: As an element, this form continues the theme of a 'lineage' or some sort of grouping. Unlike the related 'thread' element, this element doesn't normally appear on the left hand side.

name: Altar
description: This element carries the meaning of 'altar'. It becomes heavily stylised when it appears on the left hand side of a kanji. It often appears in kanji associated with spirtuality, blessings and taboos.

name: Cow
description: Another element that shape-shifts significantly. When this element appears on the left hand side, the second horizontal stroke because slightly diagonal and the order of the final two strokes switches. When this element appears at the top of the kanji, the second horizontal stroke once again forms the final stroke and the central vertical stroke does not pass all the way through it. As an element, keep the idea of 'cow' in mind.

name: Bloody Knife
description: This element is a pictogram of a bloody knife, the two final strokes represent the blood running down the edge of the knife. This element acts as a rare standalone kanji which originally had the meaning of 'not' or 'must not'.

name: Insect
description: As an element, keep the idea strictly to that of 'insect'. We will see a different element used for 'snake' later.

name: Wind
description: It is hard to draw a pictogram for the wind, so here we see the outline of something like a baloon or sail being blown out from the bottom. The form of the hooking tail changes slightly depending on the kanji.

name: Boat
description: This form keeps the meaning of 'boat'. It is used for kanji associated with boats and navigation.

name: Saw
description: Our first tool-based element is a 'saw'. The form starts with 'lie down', then the handle is represented by a vertical stroke. Finally, two horizontal strokes represent the teeth of the saw.

name: Shelf
description: Another tool-related element is the shelf. It is identical to 'eye' if not for the final stroke which is longer and forms the stable foundation for the shelf.

name: Craft
description: However you choose to visualise this element, it maintains the meaning of 'craft'.

name: House
description: This element represnets the roof of a house but will stand in for the general meaning of 'house'. You can see the eaves at the sides and even the chimney poking out of the top.

name: Hole
description: This combination of elements continues the meaning of a 'hole'. When this element appears at the top of the kanji, the final two strokes a morphed into the 'human legs' element we have seen in the kanji for Four.

name: Earth
description: When using this form as an element, this form is associated with the 'earth', 'soil' and such things.

name: Nail
description: As an element, when the idea of 'street' feels difficult to encorporate into a mnemonic, see this form instead as a nail., .

name: Possible
description: We will meet the kanji of the same form later. But for now, it is indeed possible to get your daily intake of iron by putting 'nails' in your 'mouth', so use this form when something is possible (though perhaps unlikely).

name: Bow
description: As an element, this form keeps the meaning of a bow.

name: Arrow
description: As with bow, keep this form's meaning as arrow when using as an element.

name: Hook
description: This element's relation to the idea of 'hook' is pretty self explanatory.

name: Straightaway
description: As an element, keep immediacy in mind, either doing something directly or straightaway.

name: First Aid Box
description: Though this element could represent any box, try to think of a first aid box to aid in mnemonic creation.

name: Sheaf
description: Let this element represent a sheaf: a bundle of flowers, wheat, herbs or some other produce held together with string.

name: Spirit
description: This is an unusual element, made up of 'lie down', 'one' and one half of 'wind'. Imagine a spirit-like being lying down on a floating platform, held aloft by a gust of wind.

name: Bound Up
description: Similar to sheaf, this element instead represent something tightly bound up or wrapped. This element either acts as enclosure, or appears at top of a kanji with a much shorter second stroke.

name: Mosaic
description: This element brings the idea of something colourful to the physical embodiment of that being a 'mosaic'. The first three strokes are somewhat unique, followed by the familiar 'hook'.

name: Broom
description: The element for a broom here is missing the handle! Thankfully, the other end of the broom is depicted in this element.

name: Spoon
description: This element represents a spoon. It is made up of a swooping drop moving from right to left and the 'hook' element we've seen before.

name: Dish
description: Other than the dish itself, you may instead see it as a dish rack with spaces ready to put dishes in. Note the similarity to the the 'shelf' element.

name: Measurement
description: As an element, if a height measurer doesn't work well for mnemonics, consider this element as a glue dispenser dispensing a drop of sticky glue.

name: Somebody
description: As an element, the idea needs to relate directly to either somebody, or a person's physical body.

name: Temple
description: As an element, keep to the idea of a 'temple'.

name: Length
description: Somewhat similar to the 'element' for measurement, this element also relates to measuring a height or a length of something. Imagine someone laying a piece of fabric flat and ironing out the creases in order to measure its 'length'. You can even see the remaining crease yet to be ironed out shown by the third stroke.

name: Brush
description: This unusual combination of strokes refers to a brush, especially one used for writing. Perhaps you can see the many bristles of the brush here represented by the main horizontal strokes in this element.

name: Sword
description: As an element, the form continues the meaning of 'sword'. The element will often change to two vertical lines when it appears on the right-hand side of a kanji and ends up looking a tad more like a sword.

name: Part
description: As an element, consider something being only a small 'part' of a larger whole.

name: Computer
description: As an element, this form visually represents a desktop computer complete with a keyboard. It might be better to consider the physical representation of computer instead of using 'hometown'.

name: Heavy
description: As an element, if the idea of 'heavy' is too broad, you may want to consider a heavy item, such as a dumbbell or a heavy stack of items.

name: Beforehand
description: As an element, focus on the idea of something happening 'beforehand'.

name: Horn
description: This kanji originally represented a 'horn' from an animal and came to refer to the 'corner' or 'angle' produced by the horn. As an element, use the idea specifically of a horn removed from an animal.

name: Bone
description: This element represents a bone and is made up of 'one' and 'evening'. We've already seen how 'moon' is often a stand in for 'flesh' or 'body part'. Now the 'evening' is representing the last pieces of flesh hanging from a single bone.

name: Death
description: As an element, keep this kanji related to the moment of death, rather than simply a deceased ancestor.

name: Candlestick
description: This somewhat uncommon element is comprised of a 'small moon', although its form looks similar to a lit candle. Use this visual when creating mnemonics.

name: Human Legs
description: This is the formal introduction of the 'human legs' element we have seen briefly before. You'll often see this element at the bottom of the kanji or suspended from another element

name: See
description: As an element, this form retains the meaning of 'seeing' something.

name: Light
description: As an element, continue with the theme of 'light' and 'light rays'

name: Origin
description: This form also recurrs as an element and will take the meaning of something's 'origin' or 'beginning'.

name: Teenager
description: Another form with human legs that recurrs. This time, use the more specific term of a 'teenager' when this form is used as an element..

name: Stand Up
description: As an element, keep the idea of 'stand up' for the meaning of this form.

name: Sound
description: This element will carry the same meaning of 'sound'.

name: Walking Legs
description: After standing up, the legs now start to go for a walk. This element carries the visual of 'walking legs'.

name: Each
description: As an element, concentrate on uniqueness or 'each'ness.

name: Animal Legs
description: This element is very similar to the 'eight' element we have encountered before. The main difference is that the size of the strokes are reduced and appear as a pair of 'animal legs' This form has already appeared as part of the 'shellfish' element.

name: Together
description: This element carries the meaning of doing something 'together'.

name: Truth
description: This recurring element also carries the meaning of 'truth'.

name: Devil Horns
description: When the short 'animal legs' appear at the top of the kanji and are angled inwards, they resemble little devil horns.

name: Neck
description: This element continues to carry the meaning of 'neck'.

name: Sprinkler
description: A sprinkler here is represnted by a rod with sprinkles of water flying off it in all directions. Occasionally, the rod itself will be absent, leaving behind just the sprinkles. Especially when it is in this form, we can consider this as 'sparkles' as well, such as sparkling beads of water.

name: Finger
description: As an element, this form can either take the usual form, or shapeshifts when it is in the left-hand position. When it takes its regular form, use 'hand', but when it takes its abreviated shape-shifted form, reduce its meaning to a 'finger'.

name: Elbow
description: The sharp angle in this element invokes the idea of an 'elbow'.

name: Pedestal
description: As an element, keep the idea of a 'pedestal'.

name: Public
description: As an element, imagine something that is open to the 'public'.

name: Shoulder
description: Going further up the arm, the 'elbow' below a vertical line here is referring to the 'upper arm' and 'shoulder'.

name: Gone
description: As an element, we will think of something that used to be with us, but is now 'gone'.

name: Infant
description: The element here refers to an 'infant' young enough to be carried on someone's shoulders.

name: Two Hands
description: This element represnts 'two hands'. Compare with the frame for 共 Together which showed 'two hands' raising something up, though the forms are different.

name: Possess
description: These two strokes represent a hand holding an object. Which stroke is the hand and which stroke is object, I'll leave up you.

name: Extend
description: This element represents a person stretching and 'extending' their limbs in order to reach for something.

name: Foot
description: As an element, this form continues its meaning of a 'foot'.

name: Ear
description: As an element, continue to use 'ear'.

name: Tongue
description: As an element, this form continues with the meaning of 'tongue'.

name: Beans
description: As an element, continue with 'beans' as the meaning of this form.

name: Teepee
description: This unusual element which appears at the top of kanji has the appearance of a 'teepee', a cone-shaped tent like structure associated with certain indigenous peoples of the Americas.

name: Shape
description: These three drops written from right to left have come to mean 'shape'. Imagine the wrinkles in a fabric or the waves in a person's hair.

name: Cliff
description: Be careful with this element. Make sure you ascribe the meaning to a sheer 'cliff' or 'cliff-face' and not to any sort of cave or cavern you might find in the cliffs.

name: Holding Hands
description: This element shows two hands holding one another and will use the meaning of 'holding hands'. Alternatively, a very popular interpretation is that this represents a 'crotch' which can also lead to some amusing and memorable mnemonics.

name: Jail
description: As an element, we will instead use this form's appearance as prison bars as the foundation of the element's keyword, 'jail'.

name: Gentleman
description: When using this element, keep to the meaning of 'gentleman'. This should prevent you from getting it mixed up with the similarly written form of 'soil'.

name: Woman
description: As an element, continue to use the meaning of a 'woman' here. You may want to pick a particular woman in your stories.

name: Child
description: As an element, continue to use 'child' or perhaps 'childhood' in your stories.

name: Big
description: As an element, keep in mind the idea of 'bigness' or perhaps a 'giant'.

name: Animal
description: As an element, this form may continue with the theme of 'dogs', especially when it is written in its original form. When it occupies the left-hand side of a kanji, the form shape-shifts and may take the more general sense of 'animal'.

name: Mending
description: We saw these strokes previous in the kanji and element for 'foot'. Here we see a slightly altered version of the kanji for 'correct' (正). Note that the final two strokes differ as if the kanji is in the process of beint mended.

name: Head
description: We have finally learned enough elements to make learning the element for 'head' worthwhile. You might notice a resemblence to 'neck', only the 'devil horns' have migrated to the bottom of the kanji and have become 'animal legs' instead. Imagine a 'ceiling' so low you might bang your Head on it, so to shorten yourself, you replace your legs with 'animal legs'.

name: Grass
description: We start our journey into the world of plants and nature with the simple 'grass' element. See the sprouts of grass coming out of the horizontal ground? This element often appears at the top of kanji.

name: Long Ago
description: As an element, keep to the theme of the kanji itself, focusing on stories that happened 'long ago'.

name: Grow Up
description: This element represents a small sprout of plant life that is 'growing up'.

name: Blue
description: As an element, continue to use the theme of 'blue'.

name: Life
description: As an element, we will continue to use the idea of 'life'.

name: Leek
description: This is 'grow up' but with another vertical stroke. The plant has now grown up and developed a full stem which we will take as a 'leek'.

name: Bonsai
description: Let the element for 'bonsai' be represented by three horizontal lines and two sweeping downward lines. This element does not bare any use to the word for bonsai in Japanese, but will serve as a useful visual mnemonic.

name: Wheat
description: We have already me the kanji for wheat (麦), but we will ascribe the meaning of 'wheat' to this element too.

name: Dipper
description: This element is a very styalised pictogram of a ladel-shaped dipper. The naming of this element references the 'Big Dipper', also known as the 'Plough', a collection of stars in the constellation Ursa Major.

name: Sprout
description: As an element, we will consider the original pictographical form of a 'sprout'ing plant.

name: Push Through
description: As an element, since we already have an element associated with words and speaking, we will instead use the idea of 'push through' or 'strike through' indicated by this form's final vertical stroke.

name: Rice
description: As an element, we will continue to use the theme of 'rice'.

name: Not Yet
description: As an element, continue to consider things that have 'not yet' had a chance to happen.

name: Bucket
description: This form's relation to a 'bucket' should be quite self apparent.

name: Mop
description: The mop goes hand in hand with the bucket. Notice this form's relation with both 'rake' and 'brush' elements, but don't get them mixed up in your mind.

name: Half
description: As an element, we will continue to use 'half'. When this element is positioned at the top of the kanji, another the vertical stroke bends to the left and an extra stroke is added bending to the right. You make consider this form to mean 'quarter' to help differentiate the forms.

name: East
description: As an element, you may want to expand the meaning of 'east' to encompass 'the east' in general.

name: Droop
description: As an element, this form may change slightly but will keep the general top strokes and the meaning of 'droop'.

name: Lose
description: As an element, relate this form to the idea of losing something physical, not losing in a sport or game.

name: Apple
description: As an elment, once again it might be easier to think of something that is red, such as an 'apple'. When this form appears on top, it is often abbreviated by removing the first horizontal stroke.

name: Feathers
description: Continute to use the theme of 'feathers' for this element.

name: Turkey
description: Next we find where the feathers came from, a 'turkey'.

name: Flute
description: You may look at this element and wonder how it relates to a 'flute'. The Komuso or 'monks of emptiness' were a class of monks known for playing the fute with a basket hat on their head. The flute they played is called a 'shakuhachi (尺八)' which is the inspiration for this element's given name. Originally, this form was used as an imperial measurement of length.

name: Horse
description: As an element, continue to consider the form as a 'horse'.

name: Animal Tracks
description: This is the animal equivalent to the human footprints we've seen before. The form is made up of a 'drop' over 'rice'.

name: Bird
description: As an element, continue to use a 'bird'.

name: Fish
description: As an element, continue to use 'fish'.

name: Pig
description: For this unique collection of strokes, we will asign the meaning of 'pig'. Its original form is a pictogram of a pig on its side.

name: Piggy Bank
description: The bottom of this element is a abbreviated form of the 'pig' element. Combining with a 'day', we get a 'piggy bank'. Imagine someone saving up each 'day' in their 'piggy bank' so that they can one day buy an actual 'pig'.

name: Scorpion
description: The distinctive first stroke of this element looks like the stinger of a 'scorpion' leading to the name we will use for this element.

name: Snake
description: This backwards S-shaped element will take on the meaning of a 'snake'.

name: Sheep
description: As an element, this form continues with the image of 'sheep' or perhaps a 'horned ram'. As with the 'cow' element, the appearance of this form changes subtly when placed at the top of the kanji by having the final vertical stroke not pass through the lowest horizontal stroke.

name: Rabbit
description: The next animal in our list is a rabbit. This form takes the form of 'bound up' to represent the rabbit's floppy ear along, a sideways 'sun' for its eyes and a pair of springly legs.

name: Pelt
description: This form continues its meaning of 'pelt'.

name: Scarecrow
description: This is an interesting arrangement of strokes including the 'grass' element and a sideways sun. We will give it the meaning of 'scarecrow' for our mnemonics.

name: Birdhouse
description: As stated earlier, this element will take on the meaning of a 'birdhouse' and will often drop the two strokes that make up 'holding hands'.

name: Someone
description: As an element, we will use the idea as a humble 'someone'. They are not particularly special or well-to-do. Feel free to give them a personal name if you wish or relate it to someone you know. The 'sun' part of this element may be replaced with another form.

name: Taskmaster
description: The next person we encounter is a strict 'taskmaster'. If it helps, imagine the first stroke as the taskmaster's whip, ready to whip the workers into shape. Once again, feel free to personalise this element with harsh taskmaster you may or may not know of.

name: Request
description: As an element, we will continue to use the idea of 'request'.

name: Porter
description: The Porter here is a quite an important figure. He is of course the 'gentleman' we have met before, and has the importnat job of carrying the very import 'drop' on his head.

name: Genius
description: As an element, think of a person who might well fit the role of a 'genius'.

name: Surname
description: There is some dispute as to what this arrangement of strokes is trying to represent. It could be a person bowing, or a person holding a tool, a decorated clan stick or something elese. Whichever interpretation you give it, this form will keep the meaning  of 'surname'.

name: Crown
description: This element represents a 'crown' and the great political power that comes with it. You may recognise it as an abbreviated form of both 'house' and 'birdhouse' without the decoration on top. Just don't mix it up with those similar looking elements.

name: King
description: As an element, this form will retain the meaning of 'king' and will occasionally also carry the meaning of 'ball' as well.

name: Main
description: For this element, you may think of either the 'main' part of something, or the personification of a 'master' over something.

name: Pinnacle
description: This element represents the idea of reaching the 'pinnacle'. You can think of it as a lofty skyscraper or an ivory tower. Basically if you can make it here, you've really made it. This element will always appear on the left-hand side of the kanji.

name: Heaven
description: As an element, we will continue the theme of 'heaven' for this form..

name: Pent In
description: This element represents a pen and the idea of being 'pent in' on all sides. We have already seen how some elements partially surround others, but this one encloses elements completely.

name: Cave
description: The element for 'cave' shares a striking similarity with the element for 'cliff' only with an extra stroke at the top. As previously warned, keep the two elements as separate as possible in your mind.

name: Lantern
description: As an element, this form will take the meaning of 'lantern' and will often forgo the two 'holding hands'. See the 'lantern'-like object hanging from the ceiling of the 'cave'.

name: Car
description: As an element, this form is used for kanji associated with 'cars' and 'vehicles'.

name: Ditch
description: Two holding hands holding some soil appears to be a pictogram of someone digging at the earth with the bare hands creating a ditch.

name: Enter
description: As an element, think of the act of 'entering' something rather than a physical entrance.

name: Exit
description: As with 'enter', you should think of the act of exiting when using this form as an element. If you must, think of an emergency exit, but don't get it mixed up with elements for 'door' or 'gates' that we will meet shortly.

name: Gate
description: As an element, continue to use 'gates'. If you wish, you can specifically use the idea of the 'pearly gates' to heaven to make the mnemonics less generic.

name: Gatekeeper
description: We have met the 'gates' and here we have a 'gatekeeper'. The gatekeeper has the body of 'heaven' and two 'devil horns' and acts as the final arbiter deciding whether you can join them in heaven or be sent to hell. You may want to extend this element to the general idea of gatekeeping.

name: Road
description: This element represents a 'road'. Unlike most enclosures, this form is written after the element it encloses.

name: Bundle
description: This element represents a sack tied up at both ends and carries the meaning of a 'bundle'. If you look at the elements, it is made up of a 'tree' and a 'mouth'..

name: Stretcher
description: Similar to the 'road' element, this form is written second and partially encloses another element. Imagine a person holding one end of a 'stretcher' as shown by the long final stroke.

name: Direction
description: As an element, we will continue to use the idea of 'direction'. You may want to think of someone who points us in the right direction, or a pointing compass.

name: Banner
description: This element is made up of 'direction' and 'lie down', but together take on the seemingly unrelated idea of a 'banner'. Do not confuse this element with a 'flag' which we will meet shortly.

name: Rag
description: These four strokes make up a 'rag'. On occasion, the second stroke will appear without its hook.

name: Laundry Basket
description: This form is a pictograph of a basket sitting on a stand. To make the basket a bit more unique, we will instead consider a 'laundry basket'.

name: Hood
description: This 'hood' encloses other elements, though it can also appear beside other elements too. Occasionally, the first stroke will be bent instead of straight as it does in 'moon' (月).

name: High
description: As an element, we will continue to consider something 'high'. You may want to use the idea of a skyscraper or another tall structure.

name: Inside
description: As an element, continue to use 'inside'

name: Meat
description: As an element, continue to use 'meat'. This element is related to the element for 'moon' (月) which we have seen can also mean 'flesh' and 'body part'.

name: Muzzle
description: An authoratarian state will put a 'muzzle' over the 'mouths' of those who try to 'stand up' for themselves. This element will refer to the 'muzzles' warn by these people.

name: Flag
description: Here is the element for 'flag' that was eluded to earlier. Though the etymology of this form is not in fact a flag, it's modern form is immediately recognisable as a rectangular shaped piece of cloth on a stick.

name: Axe
description: This element is a pictogram of an 'axe' with the first two strokes representing the axe's blade.

name: Door
description: The difference between the element for 'door' and the previously encountered 'flag' element is a single stroke. As with other similar elements like 'crown' and 'house' or 'cliff' and 'cave', keep the two ideas separate in your mind.

name: Clothes Hanger
description: We have seen this single stroke here and there as part of other elements such as in 'sword' (刀) and 'power' (力). We will occasionally see this single stroke appear as an element, which we give the keyword 'coat hanger' here.

name: Clothes Line
description: As an element, we can continue to use the concept of 'dry' or 'drying' or the previously mentioned 'clothes line'.

name: Towel
description: This element also represents a piece of cloth hanging on a pole. To differentiate it from the previous element, we will give this element the keyword of 'towel'.

name: Spear
description: This element appears similar to the abbreviated form of the 'sword' element, however this form's second stroke is curved instead of going straight down. As an element, we will consider this form as a 'spear'.

name: Long
description: As an element, we will continue to use the idea of 'long'. The form changes when this character appears on the left-hand side, with the bottom part taking on the appearance of 'shoulder'. This perhaps better exemplifies the earlier image of a person with long shoulder-length hair.

name: Slingshot
description: We will give these two abstract strokes the idea of a 'slingshot'. The direction of the first stroke can change directions depending on kanji.

name: Net
description: This element, which often appears at the top of a kanji, represents a latticed 'net'.

name: Scarf
description: This collection of strokes represnts a 'scarf'. It's a 'rag' that keeps 'dirt' from getting in your 'mouth'.

name: Cloud
description: An elbow under a ceiling will represent a highly styalised pictogram of a 'cloud'.

name: Weather
description: As an element, we will extend our vision to 'weather' as well as 'rain'. When this form acts as an element, the form becomes compressed and occupies the position at the top of the kanji, with the 'hood' morphing into a 'crown'.

name: Cliffhanger
description: This element appears to show someone hanging precarious at the edge of a cliff and will be given the keyword 'cliffhanger' or 'on the edge of a cliff'. You should be familiar with some of the strokes of the internal element from 'long' (長).

name: Umbrella
description: This element is related to the 'person' element (人). To help differentiate it from 'person' we will give it the unique keyword of 'umbrella'. This form often appears at the top of the kanji and above other elements as if providing shelter.

name: Fit
description: As an element, continue with the idea of 'fit' and 'fitting in'.

name: Clock
description: When used as an element, this form will take the less abstract keyword of a 'clock'.

name: Metal
description: As an element, much as how the kanji for Rain could be generalised into 'weather', this form will be generalised to cover 'metals' in general.

name: Silver
description: This element has a similar form to 'long' (長) and will be given the keyword 'silver'.

name: Eat
description: As an element, we will continue to use 'eat'.

name: Anvil
description: As an element, continue with the idea of 'bending' something and cement this idea with the physical picture of an 'anvil'.

name: Circumference
description: This form will continue to use 'circumference'.

name: Screwdriver
description: To make this element seem less abstract, we will use the idea of a physical 'screwdriver' that can be readily utilised, when considering this form as an element.

name: Seal
description: Will give this form the keyword 'seal' referring to the act of sealing something. Perhaps it resembles the lid of a jar, an ancient magical seal never to be broken.

name: Sickness
description: If you stay all night in an 'icy cave', you're bound to catch some sort of 'sickness'. This element will be primarily be used for kanji associated with sickness and disease.

name: Beggar
description: As an element, we will focus on the idea of lacking something and consider a 'beggar'.

name: Hammer
description: This element appears to represent the head of a 'hammer', one side for hitting and one side for prizing things away represented by the 'drop'. In cases where the 'drop' is absent you may think of it as a 'double-sided hammer' if this helps.

name: Valley
description: As an element, continue with the visual of a valley.

name: River
description: As an element, continue to use the visual of a 'river'.

name: Angel
description: This element appears to be an altered form of 'high' (高). We will give this rare element the keyword 'angel', a being from up 'high'.

name: Bottle
description: Here we have a pictogram of an old 'bottle' complete with a lid. The line inside the bottle indicates some of the liquid still inside.

name: Flat
description: As an element, continue with the idea of 'flat'.

name: Morning
description: A 'ten' on top of the element for 'early' indicates the period of time before 'ten' o'clock, otherwise known as the 'morning'.

name: Capital
description: As an element, continue with 'capital'.

name: Market
description: As an element, we will continue with 'market'. Think of a busy marketplace.

name: Schoolhouse
description: We saw previously a related element in 'birdhouse'. This form looks the same aside from the large top stroke. We will give this element the name of 'schoolhouse'.

name: Centre
description: As an element, we will continue to use 'centre'.

name: Crossing
description: As an element, we will extend the abstract idea of 'going' to a 'crossing'.

name: Cocoon
description: This form is an abbreviated form of the 'thread' element without the three strokes at the bottom. We will consider this form as a 'cocoon'.

name: Missile
description: This element seems to display a heavy 'missile' of sorts that takes a pair of 'holding hands' to throw into the 'wind'. We will give this element the meaning of 'missile'.

name: Run
description: As an eleemnt, continue to use 'run'.

name: Suburb
description: You may be confused by seeing this element, thinking that we had already covered it. Indeed, the form is identical to the lofty 'pinnacle' element we saw previously, but when this form appears on the right of a kanji, its meaning will shift entirely to represent the lowly 'suburbs'.

name: Sentence
description: As an element, we will extend the meaning to a whole 'sentence'.

name: Ceremony
description: This form will acquire the keyword 'ceremony'. It's appearance seems to resemble a pair of scissors cutting a ribbon, with the cut represented by the drop in the top-right corner. This element originally represented a sharp peg but has morphed considerably from its original form.

name: March
description: The 'ceremony' element here has several more strokes attached to it. A 'ceremony' with lots of bells and whistles will inevitably turn into a whole 'march'.

name: Party
description: What 'party' is complete without an 'altar'. The element at the top visually represents the bunting that goes along with the 'party'.

name: Stamp
description: This element represents a 'stamp', as in the kind you would add to a letter.

name: South
description: As an element, continue to use 'south' or perhaps the global 'south'.

name: West
description: As an element, continue to use 'west' or perhaps the wild 'west'.

name: Fur
description: As an element, use the idea of 'fur', especially animal 'fur'.

name: Noon
description: As an element, cotinue to use 'noon', and try to keep it separate from 'day' (日). Don't confuse this form with 'cow' (牛) which of course includes the head poking out of the top.

name: Chandelier
description: This rare element appears dangling over other elements and will get the keyword 'chandelier'.

name: Happiness
description: As an element, concentrate on the feeling of 'happiness'.

name: Anti
description: As an element, this form will continue with 'anti', meaning something that is opposed to something else.

name: Good
description: As an element, use 'good' or perhaps a 'good guy'.

name: Lamb
description: We will use this elemeny to help us form two further elements. The element represents a 'sheep' with one fewer horizontal stroke which we will give the keyword 'lamb'.

name: Climax
description: As an element, use the idea of a momentous 'climax'.
